attributes.name: Priority
attributes.helptext: Prioritisation can be used to arbitrate responses to multiple hits. The character's hit reaction will be interrupted and retargeted to respond (eg. reach for wound) on a shot with higher priority than the current one. So the character may reach for a head wound interrupting a reach for torso but not the other way around.

attributes.name: ReachDelay
attributes.helptext: The time delay before a reach for wound.

attributes.name: ReachDuration
attributes.helptext: This is the time the character should spend reaching for a wound.

attributes.name: MaxReachSpeed
attributes.helptext: The maximimum speed the hand should attain whilst reaching. In m/s on the standard character

attributes.name: ReflexAnimStart
attributes.helptext: The time delay between the arrival of a hit and the animated reflex response.

attributes.name: ReflexAnimRampDuration
attributes.helptext: Duration of blend in to reflex animation.

attributes.name: ReflexAnimFullDuration
attributes.helptext: Time spent holding the reflex animation at full strength.

attributes.name: ReflexAnimDerampDuration
attributes.helptext: Duration of blend back from reflex animation.

attributes.name: ReflexAnimMaxWeight
attributes.helptext: The maximum weight to be applied to the reflex animation (on a scale of 0 to 1).

attributes.name: ReflexLookDuration
attributes.helptext: This is the time the character should spend looking at either the wound or the shot source.

attributes.name: DeathTriggerDelay
attributes.helptext: Delay between setting of the death trigger and initiation of the death response (strength ramp-down).

attributes.name: DeathRelaxDuration
attributes.helptext: Duration of the death relax (strength ramp-down).

attributes.name: ShotPartImpactMagnitude
attributes.helptext: Magnitude of bullet impulse to be applied locally to the rig part. In kg.m/s on the standard character.

attributes.name: ShotBodyImpactMagnitude
attributes.helptext: Magnitude of bullet impulse to be applied globally to the rig as a whole. In kg.m/s on the standard character.

attributes.name: ShotTorqueMultiplier
attributes.helptext: Multiplier to allow modulation of angular response. The response to the bullet impact can be exaggerated (using values > 1) or attenuated (using a value between 0 and 1)

attributes.name: ShotLiftBoost
attributes.helptext: A vertical impulse most commonly used to reduce contact and the resulting friction between the character and the ground. Allows a shot impulse to flip or spin the character more easily. In kg.m/s on the standard character.

attributes.name: ShotImpulseYield
attributes.helptext: A value between between 0 and 1 sets the spine damping to be in effect when the bullet impulse is applied. A value closer to zero will make the spine react more to a given impulse, while a value closer to 1 will make it react less.

attributes.name: ImpulseYieldDuration
attributes.helptext: The duration of the spine yield following application of the shot impulse.

attributes.name: ImpulseBalanceErrorMagnitude
attributes.helptext: Stagger velocity applicable at point of impact. Can be used to exaggerate response to the shot by making the character step. In m/s on the standard character.

attributes.name: ImpulseBalanceErrorDuration
attributes.helptext: Duration of the stagger due to bullet impact. Will effect how long the character steps for after the impact.

attributes.name: BalanceAssistance
attributes.helptext: Level of auxilliary balance assistance. A means to increase the likelyhood of the character remaining standing despite the impact of a shot. Small values between 0 and 1.5 can be useful in extreme cases but higher values may not look natural.

attributes.name: ImpulseLegStrengthReduction
attributes.helptext: Amount between 0 and 1 to degrade the leg strength (balance and stepping capability) when the shot hits the particular leg.

attributes.name: ImpulseLegStrengthReductionDuration
attributes.helptext: Duration of leg weakening due to shot.

attributes.name: ShotDeathBalanceErrorMagnitude
attributes.helptext: Stagger velocity applicable as death relax begins. Induces stepping, which can be useful to produce a good fall and avoid ragdoll-like crumpling.  In m/s on the standard character.

attributes.name: ShotDeathBalanceStrength
attributes.helptext: Overall body strength at start of death relax.

attributes.name: ReachSku
attributes.helptext: Determines which arms reach for wound: 0 for left arm only, 1 for right arm only, 2 for both.

attributes.name: ReflexAnim
attributes.helptext: Id of the reflex animation applicable for this type of shot.

attributes.name: ReachSwitch
attributes.helptext: Enables or disables reach for wound reflex.

attributes.name: ReflexAnimSwitch
attributes.helptext: Enables or disables animated reflex.

attributes.name: ReflexLookSwitch
attributes.helptext: Enables or disables look at wound or shot source reflex.

attributes.name: ForcedFalldownSwitch
attributes.helptext: Enables or diables a forced fall down (to guarantee that the character falls over as part of it response to the shot).

attributes.name: TargetTimeBeforeFalldown
attributes.helptext: Target amount of time before the character should fall down in response to the hit.

attributes.name: TargetNumberOfStepsBeforeFalldown
attributes.helptext: Target number of steps the character should be allowed to take before falling down in response to the hit.
attributes.displayName: Target step count before fall down

attributes.name: ImpulseDirWorldOrLocal
attributes.helptext: Direction of impulse determines direction of any induced stepping responses. When this flag is set direction is fixed relative to the world and character staggers uniformly. Otherwise, direction follows the part that was hit and stepping follows changes in orientation of the part. The former is more commonly used while the latter may be used to simulate loss of sense of equilibrium due to a head impact.
attributes.displayName: Impulse direction fixed or follows character

attributes.name: LookAtWoundOrShotSource
attributes.helptext: If the look reflex is enabled this toggles the look target. If set the character looks at the wound, otherwise the character looks at the source of the shot.
attributes.displayName: Reflex look at wound or shot source

attributes.name: DeathTrigger
attributes.helptext: Enables or disables death response to the hit.

attributes.name: DeathTriggerOnHeadshot
attributes.helptext: Enables or disables death response for hits to the head.
